provenance.source: GitHub workflow job logs, run/jobs API, independently downloaded artifact ZIP, genuine hosted sandbox Checkout observation and selected independent Stripe GET readbacks
provenance.scenarioTiming: LIVE_READY and LIVE_WAITING were streamed during execution. The final proof step reprinted collected scenario markers after execution; those final marker timestamps are not individual payment, preparation, release, cancellation, recovery or cleanup action timestamps.
provenance.retainedEvidence: Complete sanitized scenario markers, JSON job markers and proof/configuration/health outputs are retained here. Independent provider readbacks contain only identifiers, status, money, period, schedule and fixture-metadata fields. Raw SQL/provider snapshots, hosted URLs, credentials, contact/payment details and full application configuration are excluded.
provenance.assertionScope: Journal states, saved intent/key/step identity, stock and ceased-control retention and exhaustive unchanged-state claims are enforced assertions in the pinned harness that passed against the deployed service/SQL implementation. They are not independently exported row-level SQL/provider snapshots. The artifact, markers and source identities were independently verified; the separate selected Stripe GET readbacks corroborate only the provider facts explicitly listed.
provenance.browserScope: The exact hosted session was submitted once using synthetic sandbox details, and its paid completion was confirmed by a direct Stripe GET. The browser returned to the configured application URL. That return page was not a fixture receipt or application HTTP/UI/login acceptance, and no action was taken on its existing workspace.

duringRecovery.note: These selected reads were made separately at the recorded times, not as an atomic provider snapshot. The schedule's released_at is a provider timestamp; the harness proof establishes the pending original command and loss-before-checkpoint position.

hostedPayment.confirmationSource: Independent Stripe GET for the exact submitted Checkout session returned complete and paid, bound to its USD 10 paid invoice and active quantity-two subscription. Browser returned from hosted Checkout to the configured application return page.
hostedPayment.role: Normal genuine hosted Checkout setup under the distinct setup command; no Checkout response loss was injected. The application return page is not fixture HTTP/UI acceptance.

outcome.setup: Normal Checkout made one customer and one session under its distinct setup UUID, with both responses returned normally and two completed steps on attempt one. Genuine hosted payment completed that exact USD 10 quantity-two session; GET-only refresh promoted exactly two private inactive whole-property dwellings with explicit listing opt-out.
outcome.preparation: A separate normal service cessation command used an eligible preview and the exact reviewed inventory hash to cease one dwelling. One create_schedule POST and one set_schedule_phases POST established the exact active 2-to-1 renewal schedule at the original paid boundary, with current billed quantity 2, pending quantity 1 and one managed dwelling. Both properties, one ceased control and the preparation journal were retained; its exact retry used no provider writes.
outcome.interruption: One genuine release_schedule POST with preserve_cancel_date:false succeeded, then its response was deliberately discarded before checkpoint completion. Target attempt one remained pending with exactly one incomplete release_schedule step, no set_cancellation step and no target recovery audit. Original saved schedule/customer/subscription intent and SQL-cased release key were retained while the provider schedule was released and the subscription detached with cancellation still false.
outcome.recovery: After natural SQL retry eligibility, attempt two GET-confirmed the original released schedule without another release POST, completed that checkpoint, then issued exactly one first-time cancel_at_period_end:true POST using the original unsuffixed cancellation key. Both target steps completed, exactly one recovered audit was retained, pending_quantity cleared and the durable result preserved the original paid-through boundary.
outcome.retries: Exact cancel, reconcileCancellation and recoverOperation retries returned the same result with no further provider writes, steps, attempts or recovery audits. Separate GET-only refresh retries preserved stable business fields, both private properties, the ceased control, setup/preparation/target journals and the original financial graph.
outcome.paidBoundary: Current paid management access remained valid in the active ending state before cleanup. paidThrough matched the original paid invoice line and subscription item period end, 2026-12-16T13:53:58.000Z. That future boundary was neither reached nor advanced.
outcome.cleanup: One DELETE canceled only the exact owned subscription with invoice_now:false and prorate:false. There was no Checkout-expiration POST or schedule-cancel POST. The complete paid Checkout, original USD 10 invoice/payment/charge chain, released schedule with original released_subscription binding, both properties, ceased control and all three command histories were retained; tenant, actor and membership were deactivated.
outcome.phaseDistinction: The saved target result retains cancelAtPeriodEnd:true. The separate post-cleanup provider state is canceled with cancel_at_period_end:false because cleanup immediately ended the disposable subscription. The original released 2-to-1 schedule remains as retained history and will not execute its future phase.

One schedule-release response lost after the real provider effect and before its checkpoint during period-end cancellation; pending original intent/key/step retained.

Original-command recovery through deployed service/MSSQL after natural SQL eligibility: no release replay and exactly one first-time cancellation write, two completed target steps, attempt two and one recovered audit.
Current paid access and original paid-through boundary before cleanup, stable exact-operation and refresh retries, unchanged original financial graph and retained stock/control/three histories.
Owned sandbox cleanup, retained released-schedule binding, unchanged protected accounts and clocks, exact worker scope and full serving configuration, independent public build/SQL health.
notAccepted: Successful set_cancellation response loss after release_schedule is already checkpointed; this is the next separate fresh case.
Application HTTP/UI or credential-login acceptance; hosted Stripe payment is genuine setup evidence only, and the configured application return page is not fixture UI proof.

Automatic-worker recovery, a whole-process crash/outage, provider idempotency-key age exhaustion, missing/conflicting provider evidence, retry exhaustion or broader authority/resource/isolation acceptance.
Natural paid-boundary execution or actual renewal, including the future 2026-12-16 boundary; no clock was advanced.
Cancellation reversal, zero-stock or other subscription-operation recovery, or a blanket BL08.11/R5 completion claim.

Preparation/failure cleanup branches such as attached-schedule cancellation, timeout/payment races, ambiguous responses or released-vs-attached cleanup races; these were reviewed offline but not exercised by this successful run.
Exhaustive webhook ordering or simultaneous-race acceptance; immutable original intent and supported event/projection invariants were asserted in this run without claiming all possible orderings.
Remaining cessation states and races under inventory item 1; natural seven-day grace and Evia audit remain outside R5 by owner decision.
